module: Verify the assessor and its scope

lesson.title: Who may assess this system?
lesson.summary: Verify the assessor's legal role and exact notified scope.

blocks: A **notifying authority** is the Member State authority responsible for procedures to assess, designate, notify and monitor conformity assessment bodies. States may use their national accreditation body for assessment and monitoring. The authority supervises assessors; it is not ordinarily the provider's product consultant.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 28, 30, 35, 39; Annex XIV

blocks: Article 28 requires impartial organisation, notification decisions by competent people different from those assessing the body, confidentiality and adequate expert staff. Authorities may not commercially offer the assessors' activities or competing consultancy. These safeguards support trust in designation; they do not themselves assess your product.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 28, 30, 35, 39; Annex XIV

blocks: A **notified body** is a conformity assessor designated and notified for particular tasks and system types. A consultant or ordinary certification business is not automatically a notified body. Article 35 provides a single Commission identification number and an updated public list of bodies and their activities; verify the actual entry and current status.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 28, 30, 35, 39; Annex XIV

blocks: **Notified scope** includes the activity, assessment module and system types. Annex XIV supplies product codes, biometric codes and technology-specific codes for applications and notification. A code for one category is not authorisation for every AI system. Match the proposed task to the current entry, not just the body's name.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 28, 30, 35, 39; Annex XIV

blocks: Annex XIV distinguishes Section A product categories, remote biometric identification, biometric categorisation and emotion recognition, plus symbolic, machine-learning, generative/GPAI-based and emerging technology codes. These are lookup categories, not a new high-risk classification test. Article 39 permits specified third-country bodies through a Union agreement and qualifying requirements or equivalent compliance; an overseas certificate alone establishes neither condition.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 28, 30, 35, 39; Annex XIV

questions.prompt: Who designates and monitors conformity assessors?

options.reason: It establishes and carries out the relevant procedures.
Sales authority does not create legal designation powers.
Consultancy is not the notifying-authority role.

questions.prompt: A consultant has an impressive certificate logo. What establishes notified-body status?

options.blocks: Its guarantee of a successful assessment.
options.reason: A guarantee is not proof of the notified role.

options.blocks: Its current designation and notified tasks.
options.reason: The legal role depends on notification, not appearance.
